findings.description: Missed PFL-POON_NAME-01. Document shows 'Proof Of Other Name: N/A', 'Document Status: Missing Certificate', and narrative states applicant 'failed to attach the mandatory government-issued certificate'. Worker gave only a generic requirement claim with no defect flag or abstention.

Basis asserts applicant 'submitted document ... under the proof_of_other_name document slot' implying valid supporting documentation, contradicting the document's own 'Missing Certificate' status — an overstatement not supported by the evidence.
Missed PFL-POON_NAME-01 (sibling of b6204160). Certificate is absent (N/A / Missing Certificate) yet worker reports no defect and does not abstain.
Basis states applicant 'uploaded supporting documentation under the proof_of_other_name slot', contradicting the document which shows the mandatory certificate was not attached.

Missed PFL-POON_NAME-02. Document is an 'Unverified Copy of Court Petition' with Seal Present: False and Court Clerk Signature Present: False, narrative explicitly notes lack of embossed seal/stamp/clerk verification. Worker flagged nothing — notably inconsistent with sibling cada542 which caught it.

Correctly detected PFL-POON_NAME-02: basis notes the submission is 'an unverified copy of a court petition without an official issuing court seal or court clerk signature'. Applicant-specific facts (names, docket, district) properly confined to basis[].

Missed PFL-POON_NAME-03. Document explicitly states 'Unverified Discrepancy: Middle initial V. in ECA report unreferenced in proof of name' plus a passport/ECA/degree name variance (Rostova/Rostoff). Worker produced only a generic requirement claim with no discrepancy flag.
Missed PFL-POON_NAME-03 (sibling). Same unresolved cross-document name discrepancy went unflagged.

Missed PFL-POON_NAME-04. Spanish-language certificate with 'Translation Certified: False', no translator affidavit, and 'informal self-translated printout' per narrative. Worker did not flag the uncertified translation defect.
Missed PFL-POON_NAME-04 (sibling). Uncertified Spanish translation lacking translator affidavit/stamp not detected.

patch_recommendations.suggested_patch: Add a mandatory defect checklist the agent must evaluate before answering: (1) declared other name present in personal history but supporting certificate absent (fields like proof_of_other_name=N/A or document_status='Missing Certificate') → flag PFL-POON_NAME-01; (2) court order/petition with seal_present=false, court_clerk_signature_present=false, or 'Unverified Copy' → flag PFL-POON_NAME-02; (3) name variance across passport/ECA/degree or an 'Unverified Discrepancy' field → flag PFL-POON_NAME-03; (4) non-English/French document with translation_certified=false or missing translator_affidavit → flag PFL-POON_NAME-04. Require an explicit defect claim or abstention rather than defaulting to the generic requirement statement.

Prohibit asserting that supporting documentation was 'submitted'/'uploaded' unless the document content substantiates a valid certificate. When fields indicate N/A or 'Missing Certificate', the basis must state the certificate is absent, not that documentation was provided.

For document-review tasks, mandate that every case emit either a defect finding (with the specific missing/invalid field) or an explicit meets-requirements determination. Reciting a citation-backed generic requirement without adjudicating the specific document against defect criteria is non-compliant. Ensure sibling documents (same content, different render) are adjudicated consistently.

rationale: Worker (gemini-3.6-flash) reliably reproduced a citation-backed generic requirement ('applicant must provide information/documentation on use of the other name') with exact citations to the completeness-check corpus and kept PII inside basis[], so citation_exactness, pii_containment, and blind_input_compliance score high across all cases. The two valid documents (828adaf9, 8d3ad759) were handled acceptably (no defect to miss). However, defect recall is the dominant failure: of 8 defective documents, only cada542 (missing court seal/signature) was detected — its sibling d89d1598 with identical defects was missed, revealing inconsistency. Missing-certificate cases (b6204160, b3fb24ac) also drew grounding penalties because the basis claimed documentation was submitted despite the document showing 'Missing Certificate'. Name-discrepancy (378ead7a, c3d9f81b) and uncertified-translation (b3510812, 4dbe04eb) defects were entirely missed despite being explicit on the face of each document. Net: strong provenance/citation discipline undermined by a systemic failure to adjudicate documents against defect criteria.
